statement: Evaluated on a real-world financial dataset containing 555,717 transactions with confirmed fraud ring ground truth, HMS-GNN achieves state-of-the-art performance with an F1-score of 0.84, detecting 33 fraud rings across varying sizes and complexities
This represents a 95 percentage improvement over the best single-scale baseline (f1_score: 0.54)

The AI contribution is a novel neural architecture with differentiable memory modules that persist and evolve entity representations over time, enabling effective modeling of long-term behavioral patterns and evolving fraud strategies

Experimental evaluation on real-world financial data comprising 555,717 transactions with a 0.52 percentage fraud rate demonstrates strong performance: an f1_score-score of 0.693 (21 percentage improvement over XGBoost), auc-ROC of 0.966, and detection of 33 organized fraud rings, 20 classified as high-risk

Evaluation on a synthetic customs benchmark at different levels of label scarcity showed that: (i) across views, performance was constrained below 20 percentage inspection and improved sharply near 40 percentage; (ii) feature-pair choice mattered, with the best pair depending on label availability; and (iii) multi-view aggregation provided the most balanced results, achieving the highest average overall f1_score while remaining competitive on auc and precision@10 percentage
